summary: Delegated retry scope: transport-swap during stream resume causing missing function-call acknowledgements
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that when their streaming client performs a transport swap (eg. switching from direct websocket to an edge fallback due to transient network loss) mid-retry, downstream tool/function-call acknowledgements are not observed by the client and appear to be lost. Impact: Duplicate side-effects risk and missing confirmations for long-running tool invocations. This affects a dedicated deployment for a healthcare customer with strict audit requirements.

Environment: Dedicated cluster in us-east, running a mixture of python and go streaming clients behind an in-house edge proxy. Customers use the SDK streaming API with function-calling enabled (per-action idempotency header in use).

Observed: After a network blip the client switches transport and resumes the stream. The SDK emits retries for pending function calls; the server shows the function executed and downstream webhook delivered (per logs), but the client does not receive the function-call ack event. This results in opaque state for orchestrations and occasional duplicate downstream operations when the client re-invokes the tool.

Expected: Stream resume + transport swap should preserve idempotency metadata and guarantee that function-call acknowledgements (or explicit dedupe responses) reach the client or are made queryable via the API.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create streaming session with function-calling enabled and per-action idempotency header set by client.
2) Initiate a long-running function call (eg. external webhook that takes 10s) from the stream.
3) During the function execution induce a transient network failure (client side) causing transport fallback: websocket -> edge-proxy -> http-stream-resume path.
4) Client SDK performs reconnect/resume flow and retries pending messages as per retry policy.
5) Observe server-side logs show function executed and callback delivered, but client never logs receipt of function-call confirmation event.
6) Client, not seeing confirmation, retries the same function call which results in duplicate webhook delivery downstream.
logs: CLIENT: [2026-03-12T14:02:11Z] stream: connection lost, attempting transport fallback
SERVER: [2026-03-12T14:02:15Z] func_call id=fc_987 executed, webhook_status=200, delivery_id=del_555
SERVER: [2026-03-12T14:02:16Z] ack_event queued to client on original websocket channel (closed)
comments: Aisha Patel (Support): Customer says duplicates observed ~2% of long-running tool calls after network flaps. Wants guidance and a mitigation/fix timeline.

Marco Rivera (SRE): Initial hypothesis: resume path does not rehydrate ack events from the old connection when transport changes; ack routing still targeted at original connection ID. Investigating router mapping logic between session_id and transport binding.

SRE (investigation): Checked broker logs — ack was routed to connection_id conn-778 which had been torn down. There is no guaranteed hand-off of inflight ack queue to new transport. Potential fix: ensure ack fanout uses session-level delivery (resume_token) not connection-level binding.

Customer (Nimbus Health): Provided example traces and confirmed they include per-action idempotency header: X-Idemp: pfx-uuid-0001. Also confirmed webhook server processed the request and produced audit entries. Concerned about duplicate patient notifications.
investigation_notes: 1) Reproduced locally with a test client that simulates transport fallback — confirmed client misses ack when connection torn down before ack fanout completes.
2) Edge-proxy code keeps connection-scoped routing table; resume flow registers new connection but does not migrate unacknowledged events queued to prior connection id.

3) SDKs (python & go) retry behavior is correct per client-side logs; they re-send requests with the same idempotency header, but server treats replay as new invocation in some edge cases because dedupe store is keyed by (idempotency_key, connection_id) not (idempotency_key, session_id).
4) Related to earlier tickets about connection-scoped state: SUP-472999 and SUP-821777 have overlapping context around stream resume and ack fanout.
resolution:
(pending) Short-term mitigation: recommend customer enable explicit confirmation polling for critical tool calls: after invoking a long-running tool, call our GET /v1/tool_invocations/<id> endpoint until final state appears and apply client-side idempotency checks before re-invocation. Also advise increasing ack_fanout_grace window on their dedicated cluster (ops change).

Medium-term fix: Engineering to change server-side dedupe key to be session-scoped (resume_token) rather than connection-scoped and to ensure ack fanout uses session delivery semantics across transport swaps. Created a tracking PR to sdk-python to better surface resume tokens and to log when ack events are lost: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/1892.

Next steps: Assign to runtime team for implementation and rollout plan. Notify customer with ETA once runtime patch is scheduled.
next_steps: - Runtime: design change to dedupe key and ack fanout (owner: @runtime-team)
- SDK: emit telemetry when resume happens and surface missing-ack warnings (owner: @sdk-team)
- Support: send mitigation instructions and sample polling code to customer (assigned: Aisha)
- Ops: evaluate increasing ack_fanout_grace on Nimbus dedicated cluster (assigned: Marco)
- Target: schedule a runtime patch in the next maintenance window and provide ETA to customer by 2026-03-16
